metadata.name: Hyperlipidaemia (dyslipidaemia)
metadata.emergency_level: Routine - but very high triglycerides risk acute pancreatitis
metadata.severity: Asymptomatic risk factor; severity is defined by cardiovascular risk and lipid levels

overview.short_description: Elevated blood lipids (particularly LDL cholesterol and/or triglycerides) that are usually asymptomatic but a major modifiable risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
overview.detailed_description: Dyslipidaemia is detected by blood testing, not symptoms. Its importance is as a driver of atherosclerosis (coronary disease, stroke, peripheral arterial disease). Management is guided by overall cardiovascular risk rather than lipid numbers alone: lifestyle plus statins (and add-on therapies) for primary and secondary prevention. Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) is an important inherited cause requiring early, intensive treatment and family screening.
overview.pathophysiology: Imbalance in lipoprotein metabolism raises atherogenic particles (LDL, remnants); these infiltrate arterial walls, are oxidised, and drive plaque formation. Very high triglycerides can cause chylomicronaemia and acute pancreatitis.
overview.etiology: Primary/genetic (polygenic; familial hypercholesterolaemia; familial combined hyperlipidaemia) and secondary (diet, obesity, physical inactivity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, chronic kidney/liver disease, alcohol, drugs such as steroids, thiazides, some antiretrovirals/antipsychotics).
overview.natural_history: Silent for years while atherosclerosis progresses; risk accumulates with duration and level of exposure.
overview.prognosis: Excellent when treated as part of cardiovascular risk reduction; untreated FH carries high premature coronary risk.

prevalence.value: Very common; a large proportion of adults have raised cholesterol. Familial hypercholesterolaemia affects roughly 1 in 250-500.

incidence.value: Increases with age and Western dietary patterns.

mortality.value: A leading contributor to cardiovascular deaths worldwide.

epidemiology.age_groups: Any age; screening from mid-adulthood (earlier if FH/risk factors).
epidemiology.sex_predominance: Both; risk profile changes for women after menopause.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Diet high in saturated/trans fats and refined carbohydrate, physical inactivity, excess alcohol (raises triglycerides).
risk_factors.smoking: Not a direct cause but multiplies cardiovascular risk and lowers HDL.
risk_factors.obesity: Strongly associated (raised triglycerides, low HDL - atherogenic dyslipidaemia).
risk_factors.diabetes: Causes atherogenic dyslipidaemia; major combined cardiovascular risk.
risk_factors.pregnancy: Physiological lipid rise; statins are contraindicated in pregnancy.
risk_factors.family_history: Strong for FH and premature cardiovascular disease.
risk_factors.genetic_factors: Familial hypercholesterolaemia and other monogenic/polygenic disorders.
risk_factors.medications: Corticosteroids, thiazides (high dose), some antiretrovirals, antipsychotics, retinoids can raise lipids.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Diabetes, hypothyroidism, chronic kidney/liver disease, established cardiovascular disease.

chief_complaints.complaint: Signs of severe/familial disease (tendon xanthomas, xanthelasma, arcus)
Abdominal pain from pancreatitis (very high triglycerides)

symptoms.importance: Diagnosed by lipid testing, not symptoms
Marker of very high triglycerides / pancreatitis risk

negative_findings.why_important: Excludes significant dyslipidaemia (repeat/context still matters for risk)

negative_findings.finding: No family history of premature cardiovascular disease or very high cholesterol
negative_findings.why_important: Reduces the likelihood of familial hypercholesterolaemia

history_questions.question: Family history of high cholesterol or early heart attack/stroke (men <55, women <65)?
history_questions.why_ask: Screens for familial hypercholesterolaemia and elevated risk

history_questions.question: Do you have diabetes, hypertension, or smoke, and what is your diet/activity/alcohol?
history_questions.why_ask: Overall cardiovascular risk and secondary causes

history_questions.question: Any established cardiovascular disease (angina, heart attack, stroke, peripheral arterial disease)?
history_questions.why_ask: Secondary prevention needs intensive lipid lowering

history_questions.question: Any thyroid, kidney or liver disease, or medications affecting lipids?
history_questions.why_ask: Identifies secondary causes to address first

history_questions.question: For women: are you pregnant or planning pregnancy?

physical_examination.examination: Look for xanthomas, xanthelasma, corneal arcus
physical_examination.expected_finding: Usually absent; if present suggests FH

laboratory_tests.test_name: Lipid profile (total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, non-HDL-C, triglycerides)
laboratory_tests.indication: Cardiovascular risk assessment; a non-fasting sample is acceptable for most
laboratory_tests.normal_range: Targets are risk-based (e.g., aim non-HDL/LDL reduction); see guideline thresholds
laboratory_tests.rule_in: Very high LDL (e.g., >=4.9 mmol/L) raises suspicion of FH

laboratory_tests.indication: Secondary causes and statin safety baseline

imaging.when_needed: Risk refinement in intermediate-risk primary prevention (per local practice)

ecg.when_needed: As part of cardiovascular assessment if symptomatic
ecg.findings: May show ischaemic changes if established coronary disease.

other_diagnostic_tests.pcr: Genetic testing for familial hypercholesterolaemia in suspected cases

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Diagnosis is by lipid profile interpreted within overall cardiovascular risk. Suspect familial hypercholesterolaemia with very high LDL/total cholesterol, tendon xanthomas, or a strong family history of premature coronary disease (use Simon Broome or Dutch Lipid Clinic Network criteria).

diagnostic_scores.value: Cardiovascular risk scores (QRISK3, SCORE2/SCORE2-OP, ASCVD) guide treatment; Simon Broome / Dutch criteria for FH.

cutoff_values.value: Suspect FH if total cholesterol very high (e.g., >7.5 mmol/L adults) or LDL-C >=4.9 mmol/L with family history; treatment targets are risk-based reductions/absolute levels per guideline.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Very high LDL, tendon xanthomas, strong family history of premature CVD
differential_diagnosis.distinguishing_symptoms: Family history of early heart disease
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any family history of very high cholesterol or early heart attacks?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Secondary dyslipidaemia (hypothyroidism, diabetes, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis, alcohol, drugs)
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you have thyroid/kidney/liver disease or take relevant drugs?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Very high triglycerides, eruptive xanthomas, abdominal pain
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Any severe abdominal pain and very high triglycerides?

diagnostic_questions.question: Is there a family history of very high cholesterol or premature heart disease, and do you have tendon lumps or eye signs?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Identify FH needing intensive treatment and family screening
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Positive -> assess with FH criteria / refer

diagnostic_questions.question: Do you have diabetes, thyroid disease, or take lipid-raising drugs?

next_best_question.question: What is your overall cardiovascular risk (age, BP, smoking, diabetes, family history), and any established vascular disease?
next_best_question.expected_answers: Low vs high risk / secondary prevention
next_best_question.branching_logic: Established CVD or high risk/FH -> statin + intensive lifestyle; low risk -> lifestyle and reassess; secondary cause -> treat it first

next_best_test.test: Full lipid profile + cardiovascular risk score + secondary-cause bloods

next_best_test.why: Very high LDL or family history
next_best_test.expected_outcome: Confirms FH and triggers cascade screening

red_flags.finding: Very high triglycerides with abdominal pain
red_flags.immediate_action: Assess for acute pancreatitis; urgent triglyceride lowering

red_flags.finding: Features of familial hypercholesterolaemia (very high LDL, tendon xanthomas, premature family CVD)
red_flags.immediate_action: Refer for FH assessment and cascade family screening

red_flags.finding: Established cardiovascular disease with untreated dyslipidaemia
New cardiovascular symptoms (chest pain, TIA symptoms)

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Suspected familial hypercholesterolaemia (specialist lipid clinic); severe hypertriglyceridaemia with pancreatitis.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Refractory dyslipidaemia despite optimal therapy; statin intolerance needing specialist options.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Acute pancreatitis from severe hypertriglyceridaemia; acute cardiovascular events.

initial_management.supportive_care: Assess and communicate overall cardiovascular risk; shared decision-making; address all risk factors together (BP, glucose, smoking).
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): Statin; Ezetimibe; PCSK9 inhibitor/inclisiran/bempedoic acid. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG238.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Mediterranean-style diet, reduce saturated/trans fats, increase fibre, weight loss, regular activity, limit alcohol, stop smoking.
initial_management.follow_up: Recheck lipids and adherence/response (e.g., at ~3 months after starting/adjusting), monitor for statin side effects; annual review.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Statins are first-line for primary prevention (risk-based, e.g., high 10-year risk) and secondary prevention (all with established CVD). Add ezetimibe and, where indicated, PCSK9 inhibitors/bempedoic acid for further LDL lowering or statin intolerance. For very high triglycerides, address cause and consider fibrates/omega-3; treat secondary causes (thyroid, diabetes, alcohol).

patient_education.home_advice: High cholesterol has no symptoms but raises the risk of heart attack and stroke over time. A healthy diet, activity, not smoking and (often) a statin tablet lower that risk. Statins are well tolerated for most people; report significant muscle pain. Keep taking them daily even though you feel well.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: ارتفاع الكوليسترول بلا أعراض لكنه يرفع خطر الجلطات القلبية والدماغية مع الوقت. يقلّل هذا الخطر الغذاءُ الصحي والنشاطُ وتركُ التدخين و(غالباً) حبة الستاتين. الستاتينات جيّدة التحمّل لمعظم الناس، وأبلغ عن أي ألم عضلي شديد. استمرّ في تناولها يومياً حتى لو شعرت بخير.
patient_education.prevention: Heart-healthy diet, activity, healthy weight, no smoking; family screening if familial hypercholesterolaemia.
patient_education.warning_signs: Chest pain, sudden weakness/speech difficulty (stroke/TIA), or severe abdominal pain - seek urgent care.

prevention.lifestyle: Diet, activity, weight management, no smoking - primary prevention.
prevention.screening: Lipid/cardiovascular risk screening in adults; cascade screening of relatives for familial hypercholesterolaemia.

evidence.evidence_level: High - large statin trials show cardiovascular benefit proportional to LDL lowering.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG238; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.

medication_options.when_to_consider: Primary prevention according to risk discussion or secondary prevention
medication_options.dose_policy: Dose is not inferred from this KB; use age, weight, renal/hepatic function, pregnancy status and the current local formulary/medicine label.

avoid_if: pregnancy/breastfeeding or active serious liver disease
use_caution_if: prior muscle toxicity, hypothyroidism, heavy alcohol use, renal impairment, or CYP-interacting medicines
monitoring: baseline liver tests; repeat as guideline directs; CK only when muscle symptoms/risk warrant
